title: First Word, Zero Copies
goal: Pick the implementation that returns the first word without allocating.
hints: The first word already exists inside `input`. Does the caller need a new String, or a view into the old one?
A returned &str borrows from the input — the signature says so, and the borrow checker enforces it.
explanation: The borrowed version is zero-copy: `split_whitespace` yields subslices of the input, so returning `&str` hands back a view into memory the caller already owns — the elided lifetime ties it to `input`. The owned version allocates a fresh String for every call; the double-copy version even clones the whole input first. All three pass the tests — correctness alone cannot distinguish API quality, which is exactly what this track trains.
